# SK2163 — Elapsed time is measured with the wall clock

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A duration is computed by subtracting an earlier clock read from a later one, using a clock that an NTP correction or a DST transition can move backwards.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |
| Supersedes | S6561 |

## Why

`DateTime.Now` and `DateTime.UtcNow` track civil time, which is adjusted; they are not monotonic. An NTP correction moves the clock by the accumulated drift, in either direction, at a moment nobody chose, and `DateTime.Now` additionally jumps an hour twice a year. A duration measured across either is wrong by that amount and can be negative, so a guard written to catch a slow operation reports a fast one, a retry backoff computed from it collapses, and a timeout either fires at once or never. `Stopwatch` reads a monotonic counter that none of this touches, and the rewrite is mechanical.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
var start = DateTime.UtcNow;
DoWork();
logger.LogInformation("took {Elapsed}", DateTime.UtcNow - start);
```

Write:

```csharp
var start = System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.StartNew();
DoWork();
logger.LogInformation("took {Elapsed}", start.Elapsed);
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **Both ends must be this process's own clock reads, and that requirement is the whole rule.** `DateTime.UtcNow - order.PlacedAt` is "how old is this order", a legitimate question about civil time that a `Stopwatch` cannot answer at all; only when the earlier value also came from this program reading the clock is the subtraction a *measurement of elapsed time*. A rule that reported any `DateTime` subtraction would fire on every date calculation in every domain model, and would be switched off before it found anything.

**The later end must be the clock read written in place.** `start - DateTime.UtcNow` is a negative duration and a different mistake; attaching this rule's message and this rule's fix to it would describe code it does not describe. Both operands must additionally have the same type, so the subtraction yields a `TimeSpan` and the replacement is type-identical. The `Subtract(start)` method spelling is matched as well as the operator, because it is the same operation.

⚠ **The fix's preconditions are the rule's preconditions, deliberately, and that is what `hasFix: true` costs.** It is a promise about every finding rather than most of them, so a shape the fix cannot repair is a shape this rule does not report: the start must be a local, declared by a plain local declaration statement with exactly one declarator, assigned exactly once, and read exactly once — by this subtraction. ⚠ **A start time carried in a field or a property is the same defect and is not reported.** Repairing it means changing a declaration every other member can read, and ADR-005 makes a Skala fix a text-edit list against one file's original source; that is a stated gap, not a judgement that the shape is fine. A local read twice — measured against, and then logged — is excluded for the same reason: the second reader would keep the old type and stop compiling.

**The fix writes `System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.StartNew()` fully qualified and retypes the declaration to `var`**, so it needs no `using` the file may not have and no type name it could spell wrongly. ⚠ **`fixIsSafe: false` even though the edit is mechanical and type-safe.** It replaces a value-type local with a heap allocation, which is a change a hot path's author should see, and it changes what is being measured from civil time to monotonic time — which is the repair, and is still a thing a person reads before pushing.
